upheld.reason: Subtracting common-policy Bellman equations separates value error from transition error, and the finite maximum comparison gives the same optimal-value estimate. The trap branch bounds the second model by the first plus its difference and uses the stated small transition error to retain a positive rearrangement coefficient.

Zero tolerance is dispatched to its separate established boundary supplier before any parameter formula, and large positive tolerance gives no bad steps. In the remaining branch optimism plus the corrected update count feed the escape reduction, retaining the additive slack-free cost and the full discount dependence.
